decision_description: During Phase 7 budget gate validation for the MSCA-PF (unit-cost) instrument, a conflict arose between two authorities. Authority (a): the budget-validation skill specification and the lump_sum_budget_planner interface_contract.json, whose default expectation (and Constraint 4 of the budget-response-validation logic) is that a validated external lump-sum response must be present in docs/integrations/lump_sum_budget_planner/received/, its absence being a blocking gate failure. Authority (b): CLAUDE.md Section 8 as amended by C1 (§8.1, §8.4, and §7 Phase 7 Purpose/Inputs/Gate condition), which makes the Phase 7 budget gate instrument-conditional by source and sanctions an internal deterministic unit-cost derivation (confirmed_months x published_rates x host_country_coefficient, byte-equal replay-checked) as the sole budget source for unit-cost instruments such as MSCA-PF. The specific issue in conflict: whether the absence of a lump-sum response in the integration received/ channel blocks gate_09 for this MSCA-PF unit-cost action. Resolution: the CLAUDE.md constitution (Tier authority priority 2) prevails over the skill specification and the interface contract (Tier authority priority 9) per the Section 3 authority hierarchy; the C1 amendment governs the budget-source determination. The applicable budget source is therefore the internal deterministic unit-cost derivation recorded in phase7_budget_gate/unit_cost_budget.json (all four line items resolved to Confirmed, unresolved_components empty, blocking_inconsistencies empty), and the absence of a lump-sum external response is not a blocking failure for a unit-cost instrument. The categorical Phase-8 block (§8.4) remains preserved and instrument-independent and is satisfied because every budget component resolves to Confirmed.
alternatives_considered: Treat the absence of a validated lump-sum response in docs/integrations/lump_sum_budget_planner/received/ as a blocking gate failure (rejected: C1 scopes the lump-sum received/ channel and its Constraint-4 blocking rule to lump-sum instruments only; MSCA-PF is a unit-cost instrument, so the lump-sum channel is not the applicable budget source).

Prefer the lump_sum_budget_planner interface contract as the governing budget authority because it is the concrete integration schema (rejected: the interface contract and the skill specification are priority-9 authorities and cannot override CLAUDE.md, the priority-2 constitution, per §3 and §15).

Internally generate a lump-sum budget estimate to fill the received/ channel (rejected as a constitutional violation under §8.3 and §17.6.7: fabricating/estimating budget figures is prohibited; the sanctioned unit-cost path is deterministic derivation, not estimation).
tier_authority_applied: CLAUDE.md §8.1, §8.4 and §7 Phase 7 (Constitutional Amendment C1 — instrument-conditional budget gate) as the governing authority, resolved under CLAUDE.md §3 authority hierarchy: the constitution (priority 2) prevails over the budget/decision skill specification and the lump_sum_budget_planner interface_contract.json (priority 9). Conflicting authorities named: (a) skill specification + Tier integration interface_contract.json (lump-sum external response required); (b) CLAUDE.md Section 8 as amended by C1 (internal deterministic unit-cost derivation for unit-cost instruments). Governing authority: CLAUDE.md C1 amendment.
rationale: CLAUDE.md §3 establishes that no lower-priority authority may override the constitution, and §15 confirms the constitution governs any conflict without exception. The C1 amendment (§8.1) records that unit-cost budgets carry no judgment (fixed arithmetic on published constants) and are byte-equal verifiable, so determinism supplies the anti-fabrication guarantee that externalisation supplies for lump-sum; consequently, for MSCA-PF the internal deterministic derivation is the sole sanctioned budget source and the lump-sum received/ channel is inapplicable. Recording this resolution durably is required because a material interpretation was made and an authority conflict was resolved: §9.4 requires decisions affecting future interpretation to be written to the decision log, §12.3 requires every resolved conflict to record the resolution method, the authority that prevailed, and the reasoning, and §13.5 prohibits holding durable decisions only in agent memory. This entry makes the budget-gate source determination auditable and traceable for downstream Phase 8 dependence on the passed gate.
